job.title: Carpenter for carports, patios, and decks

job.title: Storeman
job.description:
Warehouse & Materials Coordinator – Building & Construction

$35–$40 per hour casual | $70,000–$85,000 per year permanent

Take ownership of material orders, warehouse stock and site deliveries in a busy construction environment.

Siteforce Recruitment is seeking a capable Warehouse & Materials Coordinator to keep materials moving from suppliers through to site. Your work will directly support construction teams by ensuring the right products arrive in the right quantities, when they’re needed.

This is a hands-on coordination role for someone who enjoys taking responsibility, building strong supplier relationships and solving problems before they affect progress on site.

About the role

You’ll manage the day-to-day warehouse and materials function, working closely with suppliers and site teams to understand requirements, place orders and coordinate deliveries. When quantities, products or schedules change, you’ll keep orders updated and everyone informed.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Ordering building materials against site requirements and work schedules.

  • Confirming product details, quantities, availability and delivery timeframes.

  • Managing order amendments, cancellations, shortages and supplier follow-ups.

  • Coordinating deliveries with site teams to support planned works.

  • Checking incoming materials against orders and resolving missing or incorrect items.

  • Maintaining stock records and monitoring materials available in the warehouse.

  • Organising materials for dispatch and keeping the warehouse safe and accessible.

  • Identifying potential supply delays early and arranging practical solutions.

About you

You’re organised, dependable and comfortable managing several priorities at once. You follow through on orders, communicate clearly and understand how a missed delivery can affect an entire site team.

We’re looking for:

  • Experience in warehouse operations, materials coordination, purchasing or a similar role.

  • Strong attention to detail when checking orders, quantities and delivery information.

  • Confidence dealing with suppliers and coordinating with site personnel.

  • The ability to adapt quickly when site requirements change.

  • Good computer skills for maintaining orders and stock records.

  • Building materials experience and a Forklift Licence are highly regarded.

What’s on offer

  • Casual employment at $35–$40 per hour, with a clear pathway to permanent full-time.

  • Alternatively, permanent full-time employment at $70,000–$85,000 per year, depending on experience.

  • A role with responsibility across the warehouse and materials function.

  • The opportunity to contribute directly to the smooth delivery of construction projects.

Apply now with your resume highlighting your warehouse, purchasing or building materials experience.

Applicants must be Australian permanent residents to be considered.

job.title: Formwork carpenter
job.description:
Commercial Formwork Carpenter

We are seeking an experienced and reliable Commercial Formwork Carpenter to join our team. The role involves constructing, assembling, and dismantling formwork systems for large-scale commercial and civil projects. You will play a key part in ensuring concrete structures are built to specification, safely and efficiently.

Key Responsibilities

  • Read and interpret construction drawings and specifications to determine formwork requirements.

  • Measure, cut, assemble, and install timber, steel, or prefabricated formwork systems for walls, slabs, beams, columns, and stairs.

  • Erect, align, and secure formwork panels, supports, and braces to the correct dimensions and levels.

  • Place reinforcement supports, void formers, and embedded fixtures within formwork.

  • Assist with concrete pours, compaction, and finishing as required.

  • Safely strip, dismantle, and maintain formwork once concrete has cured.

  • Operate a range of hand tools, power tools, and equipment associated with formwork carpentry.

  • Maintain and repair formwork systems for ongoing use.

  • Work collaboratively with supervisors, engineers, and other trades to meet project timelines.

  • Adhere to all workplace health and safety requirements, including the correct use of PPE and safe work practices.

Skills and Requirements

  • Proven experience as a Formwork Carpenter in commercial  construction.

  • Strong understanding of formwork systems, concrete structures, and construction processes.

  • Ability to read and interpret technical drawings and plans.

  • Competent in the use of hand tools, power tools, and construction equipment.

  • Physically fit, reliable, and safety-focused.

  • White Card and relevant trade qualifications 

  • Benefits

    • Consistent, long-term project work across commercial sites

    • Opportunities for career progression and training.

    • Supportive team culture and safe working environment.

job.title: Estimator
job.description:
Estimator – Walling, Cladding & Flooring Systems
South East Queensland

This opportunity suits someone with residential construction estimating experience who understands trade packages, can interpret drawings accurately and produces clear, commercially sound pricing.

About the Role

  • Complete quantity take-offs for materials, installation and associated finishes.

  • Prepare estimates covering materials, labour, subcontractors, equipment and access requirements.

  • Obtain and assess supplier and subcontractor quotations.

  • Identify missing information, scope gaps and pricing risks, and raise queries before submission.

  • Prepare clear quotations detailing inclusions, exclusions and assumptions.

  • Liaise with builders, suppliers and internal teams to clarify project requirements.

  • Price variations and revised scopes as drawings or site requirements change.

  • Maintain current pricing information and estimating records.

  • Previous estimating experience within residential construction or a specialist trades business.

  • A practical understanding of construction methods, sequencing and labour requirements.

  • Experience estimating AAC panels, walling, cladding, rendering or flooring packages would be highly regarded.

  • Strong numerical skills, attention to detail and commercial awareness.

  • Confidence using estimating software, digital take-off tools and Excel.

The Opportunity

Work closely with construction and operations teams in a specialist business supporting residential and commercial builders. Your estimates will help secure work and give delivery teams a clear, accurate scope from the outset.

Apply Now

Supervisor: $130,000–$140,000 + Super | Permanent Full-Time
Supervisor: $65 per Hour + Super | Casual Contract
Plasterer: $37–$45 per Hour + Super | Full-Time
Immediate Starts Available

Siteforce Recruitment is seeking experienced Commercial Plastering Supervisors and Plasterers to join an established plastering and carpentry company working on commercial projects in Toowong and Sunnybank, Brisbane.

These opportunities suit construction professionals with experience delivering commercial ceilings, partitions, plastering and fitout packages.

Commercial Plastering Supervisor

Take responsibility for the day-to-day delivery of commercial plastering packages, coordinating trades and subcontractors while keeping work on program, maintaining quality and managing costs.

This is a senior, hands-on leadership role available on either a permanent full-time or casual contract basis.

Key Responsibilities

Project Delivery and Programming

  • Manage the daily delivery of assigned ceilings, partitions, plastering and fitout packages.

  • Read architectural and engineering drawings and set out wall and ceiling framing.

  • Confirm lines, levels and set-outs before work proceeds.

  • Coordinate labour, subcontractors, materials and deliveries to meet the builder’s program and lookahead schedules.

  • Organise site access, hoisting, cranage and material handling across multiple levels.

  • Identify design issues, variations and potential delays early, resolving issues before they affect following trades.

Quality Control

  • Manage Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs) for framing, insulation, noggins, door frames, sheeting and setting.

  • Inspect work before it is closed or covered, managing hold points and required sign-offs.

  • Ensure fire-rated, acoustic and seismic systems are installed to specification.

  • Maintain photographic and video records of concealed and critical works.

  • Identify defects early and coordinate rectification to achieve a consistent, high-quality finish.

Subcontractor and Builder Coordination

  • Coordinate subcontractors across framing, sheeting, setting, insulation and external works.

  • Confirm scope, pricing and program requirements before work starts.

  • Monitor productivity, workmanship, conduct and safety.

  • Maintain accurate daily timesheets and site records.

  • Review subcontractor invoices and progress claims against completed work.

  • Build strong working relationships with the builder’s site team, Project Manager and Contract Administrator.

  • Attend coordination and progress meetings and respond promptly to site requirements.

  • Document drawing clashes, design errors and preceding trade defects.

Commercial and Cost Control

  • Identify and document variations promptly.

  • Complete dayworks records for work outside the contracted scope and obtain the builder’s signed approval.

  • Support monthly progress claims by confirming completed work.

  • Monitor hired equipment and arrange its return when no longer required.

  • Record damage and delays caused by other trades to support back-charges.

  • Protect project margins through accurate documentation and cost awareness.

Safety and Compliance

  • Ensure workers and subcontractors complete inductions and follow current Safe Work Method Statements (SWMS).

  • Enforce PPE, exclusion zones and safe work practices.

  • Maintain plant, equipment, electrical testing and tagging records.

  • Ensure site first-aid requirements are maintained.

  • Report incidents, injuries and safety concerns promptly.

  • Lead by example and maintain professional standards on site.

Skills and Experience

  • Proven experience supervising commercial plastering, ceilings, partitions and fitout packages.

  • Strong understanding of construction sequencing, programming and trade coordination.

  • Ability to read drawings and accurately set out work.

  • Sound knowledge of ITPs, hold points and quality-control procedures.

  • Experience with fire-rated, acoustic and seismic systems.

  • Confidence managing subcontractor scope, pricing, productivity, quality and safety.

  • Commercial understanding of dayworks, variations, back-charges and progress claims.

  • Strong leadership, communication and problem-solving skills.

  • Current White Card and valid driver’s licence.

  • Relevant trade qualification and QBCC contractor or site supervisor licence highly regarded.

  • Available to start immediately or at short notice.

Salary and Benefits

Permanent Full-Time

  • $130,000–$140,000 + superannuation

  • Company phone, fuel card and laptop or iPad

  • Long-term career opportunity

Casual Contract

  • $65 per hour + superannuation
